entries.hypothesis: The 0.052 margin over the baseline was being diluted by low-volume players whose own recent average is already close to the best guess. Projecting fewer of them should raise the margin.
entries.change: Publish only players averaging at least 4 PPR points over their last five games. Four is the smallest cut-off that clears the 0.15 bar, and the margin rises steadily across all six scoring tiers, so it is not a threshold fitted to one number.
entries.reason: Margin over the baseline rose from 0.052 to 0.159 on 8,464 of 12,388 player-games, with coverage unchanged at 0.798. It is judged on margin because the two groups of players differ. Better players are more variable, so raw mean error rises (4.463 to 5.278) even though the margin improved.

entries.hypothesis: If low-volume players aren't worth publishing, the model might also learn better without them, since it would stop fitting an easy near-zero group.
entries.change: Exclude players below the publishing threshold from the training set as well.
entries.reason: The opposite happened. Training on everyone scored 5.266 against 5.278 on identical graded rows, so the extra rows help. Rejected, and training stays on everyone.

entries.hypothesis: Training on everyone lowered interval coverage to 0.778. Split conformal prediction needs the calibration set to resemble what is being predicted, and low-volume players have unusually small errors. Calibrating on the published players should restore coverage without changing the projections.
entries.change: Calibrate the ranges on the published players only.
entries.reason: Coverage went from 0.778 to 0.797 while mean error stayed identical to four decimal places, so only the ranges changed. They are about 0.3 points wider.

entries.hypothesis: The model sees recent form and season average as separate numbers but cannot easily express their ratio, because trees split on thresholds. Stating 'hot or cold relative to himself' directly should help more than either number alone.
entries.reason: only 0.000 better, which is within the 0.05 noise margin
